<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="אלול_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518920245_theRebbe_641" batchId="meluket-_D7_90_D7_9C_D7_95_D7_9C_meluket__BH_POST_1766518920245_theRebbe_641__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the two opposite aspects of Shabbat: that it receives from the six weekdays as Malchus, yet also blesses them after its ascent.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And it can be said that this is also the explanation of what is brought</t>
    <t s="2">(at the beginning of the maamar)</t>
    <t s="3">two extremes regarding the matter of Shabbat,</t>
    <t s="4">that Shabbat is called a queen, which is the Sefirah of Malchus that is lower than all the Sefiros and receives from them,</t>
    <t s="5">as per the statement</t>
    <t s="6">"The moon has nothing of its own,"</t>
    <t s="7">[and as per the statement of our sages, of blessed memory,</t>
    <t s="8">(regarding Shabbat)</t>
    <t s="9">"Only one who toiled on Erev Shabbat will eat on Shabbat"],</t>
    <t s="10">and on the other hand, "all the days are blessed from Shabbat,"</t>
    <t s="11">meaning that not only is Shabbat holy from all the days,</t>
    <t s="12">but moreover,</t>
    <t s="13">it influences them.</t>
    <t s="14">However, the explanation is,</t>
    <t s="15">that the seven days of the week are the seven days of construction,</t>
    <t s="16">for the six weekdays are in Zeir Anpin, as it is written,</t>
    <t s="17">"Six days did Hashem make the heavens and the earth," and it is brought in the Zohar,</t>
    <t s="18">"Each day does its work,"</t>
    <t s="19">and Shabbat is Malchus</t>
    <t s="20">(as above).</t>
    <t s="21">Therefore,</t>
    <t s="22">from this aspect, that Malchus descended below,</t>
    <t s="23">and especially from the aspect of its descent into Biyah, "her legs descend" etc.,</t>
    <t s="24">Shabbat</t>
    <t s="25">(Malchus)</t>
    <t s="26">receives from the six weekdays</t>
    <t s="27">(Zeir Anpin),</t>
    <t s="28">which is the matter of the work of refinement</t>
    <t s="29">(the refinement of the Nefesh HaBahamis and all physical things)</t>
    <t s="30">of the six weekdays.</t>
    <t s="31">However, after</t>
    <t s="32">(and through)</t>
    <t s="33">this work, there is accomplished</t>
    <t s="34">(on Shabbat)</t>
    <t s="35">the ascent of Malchus from Biyah until its ascent to its source and origin,</t>
    <t s="36">and then it ascends above Zeir Anpin until it also influences all six weekdays</t>
    <t s="37">(Zeir Anpin),</t>
    <t s="38">for "from it all the days are blessed."</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the verse "Come my beloved to greet the bride," as the drawing down of Zeir Anpin into Malchus, which also elevates the receiver to become a crown for the giver.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">7)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is "Come my beloved to greet the bride; let us welcome the face of Shabbat,"</t>
    <t s="2">which is the request of the Neshama of Yisrael that there be a drawing down of Zeir Anpin into Malchus.</t>
    <t s="3">For the beginning of the drawing down is "Come my beloved to greet the bride,"</t>
    <t s="4">a mere going,</t>
    <t s="5">and through this "let us welcome the face of Shabbat,"</t>
    <t s="6">which is the inner drawing down,</t>
    <t s="7">"the face of Shabbat,"</t>
    <t s="8">that reveals the aspect of the innerness of Malchus, even as it is rooted in Atik.</t>
    <t s="9">And therefore "let us welcome" is in the plural,</t>
    <t s="10">for Zeir Anpin also receives from</t>
    <t s="11">(the root of)</t>
    <t s="12">Malchus,</t>
    <t s="13">"a woman of valor is the crown of her husband."</t>
    <t s="14">And just as it is above in Zeir Anpin and Malchus,</t>
    <t s="15">so too is it with every influencer and receiver,</t>
    <t s="16">that through the receiver, addition is brought to the influencer,</t>
    <t s="17">and "from my students more than from all of them."</t>
    <t s="18">And especially with a groom and bride below,</t>
    <t s="19">that specifically through the inner drawing down,</t>
    <t s="20">behold "a woman of valor is the crown of her husband,"</t>
    <t s="21">and "everything was from the dust."</t>
    <t s="22">For through this, the power of Ein Sof is drawn down, "a generation of the upright shall be blessed," with sons and grandsons engaged in Torah and mitzvos.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
